source_policy: Primary references support definitions and stated conditions. Scenarios and worked derivations are originally authored constructions. The supplied book matrix guides sequencing; it is not independent verification of exact-edition book coverage.
purpose: Which regular tile corners meet without a gap or overlap?
meaning: At a regular convex n-gon corner, the interior angle is α=180(n−2)/n degrees. Bringing q such corners together leaves signed gap g=360−qα degrees. Positive gap leaves uncovered angle and negative gap means angle overlap. The tested regular plane tilings use six triangles, four squares or three hexagons at every vertex. A local angle equation alone is not a general tiling theorem.

definition.setting: A floor designer brings q equal corners from regular n-sided tiles to one point. Follow each interior angle into the full turn, then compare the three regular plane tilings.

signature.n: Whole number of sides of each regular convex tile
signature.q: Whole number of tile corners brought to the same vertex
signature.g: Signed remaining full-turn angle, in degrees

conditions: Use a whole side count from three through twelve and whole corner count from two through six, in the Euclidean plane. Congruent convex regular polygons are assumed. The signed gap describes this local vertex; only the compatible triangle, square and hexagon cases show a plane-tiling patch.
definition.domain_notes: Use whole sides n from 3 to 12 and whole copies q from 2 to 6. Positive g is a gap and negative g is angle overlap. Local angle compatibility is necessary, not a general proof that an arbitrary tile covers a plane. For the regular convex polygons tested here, the compatible pairs are triangles six at a vertex, squares four, and hexagons three. Those three cases also show a finite patch of their actual Euclidean plane tiling.
